title: ScVal map with keys U32(1), String("1") and Symbol("1"), which collide as native text keys
why: The three keys are distinct ScVals in host order, so the map is valid on chain, but they collapse to one or two native key(s) in a language whose maps are keyed by text or by a loosely typed value. A converter must keep all three entries or refuse; silently keeping fewer loses data.

source.reason: A bare ScVal built by hand from the XDR definitions; a contract can return or emit it, but these bytes were not taken from core output

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 17.2.0 and 17.2.1: scValToNative returns an object with 1 key(s) and no error. 17.3.0 and later throw 'scvMap has more than one key that converts to …'. Earlier 17.x versions were not run.
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 4a (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on js 17.2.0 and js 17.2.1; xcc conform run --columns 'js@17.2.*' --entries 'cap-0046/scval-map-keys-collide-three-types.u32-string-symbol'

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1 and 16.4.1: scValToNative returns an object with 1 key(s) and no error; the fix of the v17 line was not backported to v16.
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 4a (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on js 16.3.0, js 16.3.1 and js 16.4.1

known_divergences.detail: scval.to_native builds a dict: the string and symbol keys "1" are equal in Python, so an entry is dropped.

notes: Probe vector 4a (evidence/sdk-matrix/vectors/vectors.json). stellar-core 30.0.0 print-xdr --filetype scval decodes it to the same three entries (run by hand for this entry).
